assertion_results.evidence: task-1 covers `src/catalog/store.py` (line 31) and `tests/catalog/test_store.py` with tests for round-trip persistence (line 94), fail-closed validation (line 95), and 'an update without `ownerGroup` keeps the stored value, and an update with a new value replaces it' (line 96). None of the test_store.py items, and none of the store.py descriptions, check that stable IDs stay unchanged. Stable-ID checks appear only in the writer tests (lines 97-100) and the general AC on line 91. Because the store-level verification of stable IDs is missing, this assertion fails under the strict, no-partial-credit rule.

assertion_results.text: Implementation tasks specify path-specific validation: registration persists the supplied ownerGroup, scheduled sync/fallback/on-demand updates preserve an existing value when omitted and apply a supplied replacement, and both consumers expose values from all four writers
assertion_results.evidence: The following parts are present. Registration: 'registering a service stores the supplied `ownerGroup`' (line 97). Fallback: 'importing exported data with `ownerGroup` stores it. Importing data without `ownerGroup` keeps the existing value' (line 99). On-demand: 'without `ownerGroup` keeps the stored value. With `ownerGroup`, it updates the value' (line 100). Consumers: lines 101-102. Scheduled sync, however, only preserves the value: 'syncing an existing record keeps its `ownerGroup`' (line 98) and 'keep the existing `ownerGroup` when synchronizing provider metadata' (line 33). Sync has no item that applies a supplied replacement value, so the requirement is not met for scheduled sync.
